status: historical 16-trajectory prototype; superseded by assumption_codebook_v1.json and not for current annotation
unit: one atomic clinical proposition; a decision step may contain several hierarchical propositions
rules: Retain the source proposition verbatim alongside every normalized code.
Assign type, level, and status to each atomic proposition, never once to the whole step.
Use multiple propositions when disease existence is established but etiology, severity, complication, or intervention state remains uncertain.
Do not infer an assumption type from modality or action_role alone.
Observed conditions such as age, pregnancy, renal function, contrast constraints, and resource availability are context unless the order is explicitly investigating them.
Use other for a coherent recurring proposition outside the listed types and preserve a free-text proposed type.
Use unclear when the proposition or its level cannot be reliably recovered; do not force it into other.

types.definition: A broad syndrome or incompletely localized anatomic process organizes the workup before one disease or finding identity dominates.
include: an intra-abdominal inflammatory or infectious process is present but its organ source is unknown
the abdominal source of sepsis, obstruction, or pain remains unlocalized
exclude: a named disease is the proposition being tested; use disease_or_finding_identity
a known disease is being staged; use severity_extent_or_course

types.definition: The existence or identity of a named disease, lesion, collection, or observed abnormality organizes the workup.
include: appendicitis is present
a hepatic collection is a biloma rather than a hematoma
pelvic lymphadenopathy is reactive rather than lymphoproliferative
exclude: what caused an already identified disease; use etiology_or_mechanism
how extensive or progressive an established process is; use severity_extent_or_course
types.origin: seed disease-existence type broadened empirically to finding identity

types.definition: A cause or mechanism of an established or strongly suspected disease/finding organizes the workup.
include: pancreatitis has a biliary cause
duct dilation is caused by a retained stone, stricture, or ampullary lesion
persistent cholestasis reflects incomplete drainage
exclude: an unrelated organ system may instead cause the symptoms; use alternative_source
whether a device is positioned or functioning; use intervention_or_device_state

types.definition: The extent, grade, response, stability, progression, or resolution of an already recognized process organizes the workup.
include: an abscess has enlarged or responded to treatment
inflammation has progressed or resolved
the current anatomic extent could change management
exclude: the possible new adverse entity itself, such as necrosis or perforation; also code complication
the base disease has not yet been identified; use disease_or_finding_identity or syndrome_or_source_frame
types.origin: seed severity type expanded empirically to longitudinal course

types.definition: A consequential adverse development of a disease, procedure, or prior finding organizes the workup.
include: perforation, abscess, necrosis, pseudocyst, fistula, bile leak, or post-procedural injury
superinfection or rupture of a known collection
exclude: size or interval response without a distinct adverse entity; use severity_extent_or_course
an unrelated competing diagnosis; use alternative_source

types.definition: A different disease, organ, or clinical frame may replace or materially compete with the focal explanation for the presentation.
include: a gynecologic, urologic, vascular, malignant, or other bowel source may explain the pain
another abdominal process may explain deterioration better than the current focal disease
exclude: a cause nested under the retained disease; use etiology_or_mechanism
a list of possibilities before any focal frame exists; use syndrome_or_source_frame and code named propositions individually when supported

types.definition: The position, patency, adequacy, effectiveness, or failure of a prior intervention or device organizes the next imaging decision.
include: a biliary stent is patent, well positioned, or adequately decompressing
a drain is positioned and controlling a collection
a prior intervention has failed or requires revision
exclude: injury, leak, bleeding, or infection caused by a procedure; also code complication
the biological cause of disease independent of the intervention; use etiology_or_mechanism

types.definition: A coherent assumption proposition is recoverable but its type is outside the provisional codebook.
include: a supported proposition with a proposed free-text type that should be audited for recurrence

types.definition: The available text does not support a stable proposition or level.
include: the order is weakly motivated or several incompatible propositions cannot be separated
exclude: a clear but novel type; use other

statuses.definition: Plausible and actively considered, but not the clear leading proposition and not adequately established.
The leading supported proposition, but still awaiting decisive confirmation.
Adequately supported by causally available evidence or explicitly documented as known; downstream uncertainty may remain at another level.
Previously active and still possible, but materially weakened by valid negative, discordant, or temporal evidence.
Sufficiently and validly refuted for the current decision point; nonvisualization, nondiagnostic study, or not-assessed anatomy is not exclusion.
The proposition is recoverable but its status cannot be assigned without overstatement.

cross_cutting_notes: Temporal qualifiers such as new, persistent, recurrent, stable, improving, and worsening remain attributes of the proposition; they are not standalone assumption types.
Anatomic target, disease identity, and intervention state can coexist in one step and should remain separate propositions.
Alternative_source is relational: state which focal proposition it competes with.
The source sample is purposive and multi-label, so assignment counts are not prevalence estimates.
